actions.action: Tap leaves/flowers over white paper to look for thrips
Inspect leaf undersides for black frass specks
Place yellow or blue sticky traps
Check flowers and new growth for hiding thrips
Patch-test the alcohol/peppermint spray on one leaf and wait 24-48 hours, or dilute it
Isolate infested plants and inspect all others
Prune, bag and discard badly damaged leaves and spent flowers
Spray every 5-7 days for 4-6 weeks with insecticidal soap or neem/horticultural oil
Alternatively use pyrethrin-based spray for knockdown
Apply beneficial nematodes (Steinernema feltiae) to the media
Release predatory mites such as Amblyseius cucumeris
Rotate pesticide products to avoid resistance
Quarantine new plants for several weeks
Check product compatibility with each orchid type before spraying
Take a close-up photo of a live insect to confirm ID

reason: The answer names thrips as the main diagnosis, but the beneficial-insect program that worked appears only as one soil-treatment option among many sprays, so the advice is partial; nothing recommended is likely to harm the plant.
